Khanna M/s Pallavi Enterprises An9B, Shalimar Bagh New Delhi110 088. Appeal Under Sections 377 Code Of Criminal Procedure Against The Order Dated 07.02.2013 Of Ld.Acmm Ii,New Delhi. Date of Institution of Appeal : 17.09.2013
texts.facts: It is submitted that as per Director CFL's report, the sample of Kaju pieces was reported to be misbranded on account of violation of rules 32 (c)(e)(f), 42 (zzz)17, of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 ("PF Rules" in short) i.e. mentioning of incomplete address, not giving batch number, best before and vegetarian symbol. The respondent has pleaded that the appeal is time barred. 4.1 It is seen that the impugned oder of se challenge in this appeal was passed on 07.02.2013. The appeal was filed on 17.09.2013 i.e. after 220 days. Article 115(b) of Limitation Act, 1963, ("Limitation Act" in short) prescribes limitation period of 30 days for criminal appeals against order of sentence. Article 115 reads as under : Description of appeal 115. But the appeal has been filed after about 220 days, that is, after a delay of 190 days. 4.2 The appellant has submitted that after receipt of certi copy of the judgment/impugned order, Ld. Addl. Public Prosecutor prepared his report on 14.02.2013. Thereafter, the Chief Public Prosecutor submitted his report to the PFA department on 19.02.2013. The file thereafter remained under consideration in PFA department. After getting the approval of Commissioner, Food Safety, the file was sent to Law Department and from there the file was sent to office of Hon'ble LG for final approval. After getting the approval of Hon'ble LG , the file was received back in the prosecution branch on 13.09.2013. Thereafter, the appeal was prepared and was sent to PFA Department for signatures by the concerned FI/FSO. On receiving the appeal after signatures it was immediately presented in the court without any further delay. The delay was caused due to the procedural formalities and was unintentional. The same was challenged by way of appeal before the sessions court and on not succeeding, the appellant filed revision petition before the Hon'ble High Court which was also dismissed. The appellant then preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
